channel.title: Carat Capital — The Trade Paper of the Jewelry World
channel.description: Prices, intelligence and analysis from every desk of the stone trade: diamonds, gold and metals, gemstones, watches, auctions, retail and technology.

item.title: Nobody has De Beers yet, and there will be no listing
item.description: Anglo American's chief executive says the sale is in its final and hardest phase, that no bidder holds exclusivity, and that a public listing is off the table. Completion is targeted for the second half.

item.title: Zero for Antwerp, and the grown stone pays anyway
item.description: The Section 301 tariffs that took effect on July 24 exempt loose natural diamonds cut in the European Union at 0%, along with coloured stones and natural pearls. Lab-grown diamonds received no exemption anywhere on the list.

item.title: The tender ladder: 100% in Dubai, 75% in Johannesburg
item.description: TAGS cleared 100% of a Zimbabwean parcel and 95% of an Angolan one this summer, but only about 75% of South African goods in Johannesburg. Its latest Dubai sale of large South African stones took $15.2 million at above 80%.

item.title: A record second quarter, the weakest half since 2022
item.description: Central banks bought 289 tonnes of gold in the second quarter, up 62% and a record for any second quarter. The first half still totalled 345 tonnes, the smallest since 2022, because the first quarter collapsed to 57.

item.title: $380 billion: the half-year that cost the most
item.description: Total gold demand held flat at 1,269 tonnes in the second quarter and rose 2% to 2,522 tonnes across the half. In money rather than metal, that half-year set a record near $380 billion.

item.title: Gold opens August at $4,041.70 and waits on payrolls
item.description: No session since Friday's Kitco close of $4,041.70, so the tape carries. The week brings the ADP employment report midweek and non-farm payrolls on Friday, into a metal six weeks into a consolidation.

item.title: NY Now opens today under new owners
item.description: The summer market runs August 2 to 4 at the Javits Center, the first edition since Rockview Management Group bought the show from Emerald. More than 70 exhibitors are new or returning.

item.title: Bain puts jewellery on top of a flat luxury market
item.description: The Bain and Altagamma spring study has personal luxury goods growing 2% to 4% in 2026, reaching €365 to €373 billion after falling to €358 billion last year. Jewellery is named the strongest category.

item.title: Russia bans the word: synthetics lose diamond, carat and natural
item.description: Government Resolution No. 657 of May 30 takes effect on September 1. Tags must say synthetic, weight must be shown in grams rather than carats, and precious, natural, real and eco-friendly are struck from the vocabulary.

item.title: Dubai sets a second Diamond Week for October 26
item.description: DMCC will run the second Dubai Diamond Week from October 26 to 29, with the Italian Exhibition Group co-hosting a sourcing show. The emirate traded a record $41.7 billion and 359.5 million carats last year.

item.title: $4,041.70: gold's first monthly gain since February
item.description: Kitco's Friday close puts gold at $4,041.70, down $60.90 or 1.48% on the day. July still finished about 0.5% higher, ending a four-month losing run, as the dollar rebounded from a six-week low.

item.title: $1,256 palladium: the white metals give the month back
item.description: Kitco's Friday close puts palladium at $1,256, down 3.38%, silver at $57.44, down 2.45%, and platinum at $1,644, down 0.60%. The gold-silver ratio widened to about 70.4.

item.title: Hermès sells €269 million of watches and calls it stable
item.description: First-half watch revenue fell 4.2% as published and rose 0.2% at constant rates. The second quarter grew 4.4%. Jewellery and home together took €1.065 billion, up 5.4%, on a group margin of 41%.

item.title: Bucherer will run Rolex's Fifth Avenue flagship
item.description: The Swiss retailer, bought by Rolex in 2023, confirmed it will operate the four-floor Fifth Avenue store. WatchPro puts it at 43,000 square feet, more than four times the current largest Rolex showroom, opening around the turn of the year.

item.title: De Beers takes Friendship Day into 60 Indian stores
item.description: The second edition of Love, from Bestie runs August 1 and 2 across 60 retail partners in nine cities, built on four paired natural diamond bracelets, one spelling BFF in Morse code.

item.title: A $1 battery, a $15 ticket: the counter's quietest margin
item.description: Sy Kessler's new battery starter kit lists from $235. The battery inside costs about $1 and the job sells for more than $15, one of the few service lines a jeweller still prices alone.

item.title: De Beers loses $188 million and points at a steady index
item.description: Anglo American's half-year accounts put De Beers revenue at $1.58 billion, down 19%, with an underlying loss of $188 million, 23% narrower. The realised price fell 32% to $105 a carat; unit costs fell 26% to $64.

item.title: $4,055 gold: Thursday's rally goes back out on a dollar bounce
item.description: Spot fell 1.19% to $4,054.68 an ounce on the last trading day of July as the dollar rebounded and traders booked the previous session's gains. Gold is still 20.57% higher on the year and about 1.4% higher on the month.

item.title: $57.99 silver, $1,636 platinum: the white metals close July lower
item.description: Silver fell 1.72% to $57.99, platinum 1.46% to $1,636 and palladium 1.53% to $1,288.50. All three are far higher on the year: silver 56.44%, platinum 24.28%, palladium 6.80%.

item.title: 278 tonnes: the smallest jewellery quarter since the pandemic
item.description: World Gold Council data put second-quarter jewellery demand at 278 tonnes, down 17% and the lowest quarterly volume since the pandemic, while its value rose 14% to $40 billion. Total gold demand held flat at 1,269 tonnes.

item.title: India's quarter: 75.1 tonnes of jewellery, down 15%
item.description: Indian jewellery demand fell to 75.1 tonnes in the second quarter from 88.8 tonnes, a 15% decline, and total Indian gold demand fell 6%. The value of that demand rose about 50% as prices set records.

item.title: 90.8: confidence slips, and the present tense is the weak part
item.description: The Conference Board's index fell 1.4 points to 90.8 in July against a 92.3 consensus. The present situation index dropped 3.6 points to 114.9, a third consecutive decline, while expectations held at 74.7.

item.title: Jewelers of America returns to Washington with one ask: exclusion
item.description: Trade groups met administration officials as a 10% to 12.5% tariff round covering about sixty countries took effect. Seven African producers and diamonds polished in the EU are exempt; India stays at 10%, and a second investigation is open.

item.title: $102.9 million, up 72%: Gemfields' emeralds cover for its rubies
item.description: First-half auction revenue rose 72% to $102.9 million. Net debt stood at $44.2 million on June 30 before $33.3 million of auction receivables, and premium-grade ruby recovery at Montepuez ran at 0.025 carats a tonne.

item.title: One billion for De Beers, and $750 million of it up front
item.description: Bloomberg puts the Gareth Penny consortium's price at about $1 billion: roughly $750 million on closing and $250 million later, with some $500 million of working capital going in behind it. Book value earlier this year was $2.3 billion.

item.title: Ninety-five percent sold in Luanda, and Sodiam beats its book by 23%
item.description: TAGS cleared 95% of a Luanda tender of goods above 10.8 carats and called trading near normal. Sodiam's seventeenth auction took about $21.7 million net from 6,586.89 carats, 23.46% above expected value.

item.title: Gold takes back $4,075 the morning after the hold
item.description: Spot recovered to about $4,074.98, up 0.22% on the day and 23.84% on the year, erasing Wednesday's post-FOMC slip to $4,029. Silver eased to $57.79 and the gold-silver ratio widened to 70.37.

item.title: Platinum jumps to $1,628 as the man who taught it retires
item.description: Platinum rose 1.62% to $1,628.20 and is 26.13% higher on the year, yet global platinum jewellery demand is forecast to contract 6% in 2026. PGI USA announced Kevin Reilly's retirement on July 28.

item.title: All four Swiss groups turn positive for the first time since 2022
item.description: Morgan Stanley's second-quarter secondary-market index rose 1.5%, with Swatch Group up 5.4% and Richemont 4.2% year on year. April was the market's best single month since March 2022 at plus 2.5%.

item.title: Heritage books $1.41 billion, and its biggest jewelry sale ever
item.description: First-half sales rose 47% to more than $1.41 billion, the highest midyear total in the firm's fifty years. Its May 4 jewelry auction made $9,713,640, led by a 6.59-carat Kashmir sapphire at $906,250.
